Why Energy Stocks Are Down When They Should Be Up with Bob Brackett | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 60

Bob Brackett explains why near-term oil cash flows, forward curves and producer equities can diverge. He favors disciplined commodity exposure, dry-gas producers, Exxon, Diamondback and Cheniere while remaining tactically cautious on copper. Eisman adopts a cyclical entry-and-exit framework. Primary evidence supports severe supply disruption, regional gas congestion and strong producer cash generation, but several long-run scenarios remain unfinished and the storage-cost explanation has the wrong sign.

youtube-dFGIXqpyVzA-c011 · analytical principle

Cheap-to-store commodities tend toward contango, whereas expensive-to-store oil and iron ore tend toward backwardation because of storage cost.

Wrong
Source · 17:19-18:41 ↗
SpeakerBob Brackett
Stanceasserted
Horizonnot stated
Materialitymajor

The storage-cost sign is reversed when other factors are held fixed. Carrying costs raise deferred prices; backwardation requires sufficiently strong convenience yield or other forces. Oil is not almost always backwardated.

Conditional reasoning

The carry relationship is F = S exp((r + u - y)T). Increasing storage cost u raises F relative to S, pushing toward contango, not backwardation.

  • A storable commodity with financing rate r, proportional storage cost u and convenience yield y.

Assessment test: Inspect the relevant original financial, operational or economic data and compare the claimed mechanism with competing explanations.

Further verification: Recheck the original data and subsequent realized outcomes.

A partial inflation-hedging rationale is plausible; equating risky equity payouts with contractual inflation protection omits material basis and equity risk.

Conditional reasoning

Commodity exposure can hedge certain price shocks, but production costs, oil demand, leverage and payout decisions can offset it. Unlike indexed Treasury principal, an oil dividend has no contractual CPI adjustment, so the yields are not directly equivalent.

  • Oil prices and company cash flows may respond positively to some inflation shocks.
  • Equity dividends are discretionary and are not contractually indexed to a consumer-price measure.

How he reasons here

  • Separate transit flows, shut-ins, inventory draws and net deficits.
  • Value equities on cash flows and capital allocation, not spot commodities alone.
  • Futures prices combine expectations, carry, convenience yield and risk premia.
  • Distinguish resource estimates from commercially recoverable low-cost supply.
  • Compare integrated, upstream, service and midstream risk separately.
  • Strong demand growth can coexist with poor supplier returns when capacity overexpands.

Tools and charts discussed

Mentioned in the transcript; visual charts have not all been inspected.

  • Oil spot and forward curves.
  • Commodity EBITDA sensitivity and net-debt bridge.
  • Mining margins across cycles.
  • Copper inventories and tariff scenarios.
  • Gas basis, pipeline constraints and associated supply.
  • FCF yields and LNG contracted capacity.
